title: introduce-rag-edge-offline-debugging-playbook
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: Teams building RAG features for edge or air-gapped devices asked for a concise, reproducible developer playbook for offline debugging, deterministic replay, and compact telemetry so they can iterate without a live Redwood Private control plane. This PR adds a docs quickstart that combines: 1) a headless 'playback runner' for replaying captured requests and token streams offline; 2) a lightweight 'compact telemetry probe' that captures minimal timing/kvcache metrics and is safe to store on-device; 3) an authoring guide showing how to take production traces, generate a deterministic offline index snapshot, and run local regressions and smoke-evals. Motivation: reduce developer turnaround time for reproducing inference regressions observed in Dedicated/Private deployments; enable teams to run deterministic acceptance tests on-device and in CI. Changes: new quickstart doc (site/docs/quickstarts/rag-edge-offline-debugging-playbook.md) with step-by-step guide and screenshots; example playback runner (examples/rag/edge-playback/playback-runner.ts) with a CLI shim for headless replay; compact telemetry probe (examples/rag/edge-playback/telemetry-probe.js) and index snapshot script (scripts/dev/generate-index-snapshot.sh); small site navigation update so this quickstart appears under "Edge & Private". Checklist: - [x] Add authoring and reproduction guide for offline traces; - [x] Include reproducible example code and small dataset; - [x] CI smoke tests for playback runner on linux/mac; - [x] Docs lint and site build pass; - [x] Confirm no secrets/KMS keys are included. Backwards compatibility: docs-only + example code; no breaking changes to public APIs. How to validate locally: follow quickstart steps to capture a short trace from a hosted session, run generate-index-snapshot.sh to create a compact snapshot, then run playback-runner.ts against the snapshot and compare token-level output to the captured trace. See release notes below for recommended follow-up tasks for teams wanting to adopt this pattern across their fleets.
